source_excerpt:
Break the chains. Free the mind. Keep the brain.
Try it now on HuggingFace Spaces — runs on ZeroGPU, free daily quota with HF Pro. No setup, no install, just obliterate.
OBLITERATUS is the most advanced open-source toolkit for understanding and removing refusal behaviors from large language models — and every single run makes it smarter. It implements abliteration — a family of techniques that identify and surgically remove the internal representations responsible for content refusal, without retraining or fine-tuning. The result: a model that responds to all prompts without artificial gatekeeping, while preserving its core language capabilities.
But OBLITERATUS is more than a tool — it's a distributed research experiment. Every time you obliterate a model with telemetry enabled, your run contributes anonymous benchmark data to a growing, crowd-sourced dataset that powers the next generation of abliteration research. Refusal directions across architectures. Hardware-specific performance profiles. Method comparisons at scale no single lab could achieve. You're not just using a tool — you're co-authoring the science.
The toolkit provides a complete pipeline: from probing a model's hidden states to locate refusal directions, through multiple extraction strategies (PCA, mean-difference, sparse autoencoder decomposition, and whitened SVD), to the actual intervention — zeroing out or steering away from those directions at inference time. Every step is observable. You can visualize where refusal lives across layers, measure how entangled it is with general capabilities, and quantify the tradeoff between compliance and coherence before committing to any modification.
OBLITERATUS ships with a full Gradio-based interface on HuggingFace Spaces, so you don't need to write a single line of code to obliterate a model, benchmark it against baselines, or chat with the result side-by-side with the original. For researchers who want deeper control, the Python API exposes every intermediate artifact — activation tensors, direction vectors, cross-layer alignment matrices — so you can build on top of it or integrate it into your own evaluation harness.
We built this because we believe model behavior should be decided by the people who deploy them, not locked in at training time. Refusal mechanisms are blunt instruments — they block legitimate research, creative writing, and red-teaming alongside genuinely harmful content. By making these interventions transparent and reproducible, we hope to advance the community's understanding of how alignment actually works inside transformer architectures, and to give practitioners the tools to make informed decisions about their own models.
Built on published research from Arditi et al. (2024) , Gabliteration (arXiv:2512.18901) , grimjim's norm-preserving biprojection (2025) , Turner et al. (2023) , and Rimsky et al. (2024) , OBLITERATUS implements precision liberation in a single command:
Or zero commands — just open the Colab notebook and hit Run All.
OBLITERATUS is an alignment research tool. It exists to advance the scientific understanding of how safety behaviors are encoded in language model weights — specifically, the geometric structure of refusal representations in transformer activation space.
Arditi et al. (2024) — discovering that refusal is mediated by a single direction
HarmBench (Zou et al., 2024) — standardized evaluation of LLM safety
JailbreakBench — tracking adversarial robustness of safety training
Anthropic's red-teaming datasets — published for reproducible safety research
By making refusal removal transparent, reproducible, and scientifically rigorous, OBLITERATUS contributes to the broader understanding of how alignment actually works inside transformer architectures — knowledge that is essential for building better safety mechanisms.
Alignment researchers studying refusal geometry, safety robustness, and mechanistic interpretability
Red-teamers evaluating how post-training safety holds up against weight-level interventions
AI safety evaluators who need unrestricted baselines for benchmarking
Local-first practitioners who want full control over models running on their own hardware
Anyone seeking to generate content that causes real-world harm to real people
Anyone without the technical understanding to use uncensored models responsibly
Models produced by OBLITERATUS have had safety guardrails surgically removed. You are solely responsible for how you use this tool and any models or content it produces.
Choosing settings? Start with Choose a workflow and the UI controls and feature-scope guide . They explain defaults, tradeoffs, memory warnings, interpretation, and which features require the CLI/API rather than the web interface.
OBLITERATUS does four things — and the community does the fifth (see Community-powered research below):
1. Map the chains — Ablation studies systematically knock out model components (layers, attention heads, FFN blocks, embedding dimensions) and measure what breaks. This reveals where the chains are anchored inside the transformer — which circuits enforce refusal vs. which circuits carry knowledge and reasoning.
2. Break the chains — Targeted obliteration extracts the refusal subspace from a model's weights using SVD decomposition, then surgically projects it out. The chains are removed; the mind is preserved. The model keeps its full abilities but loses the artificial compulsion to refuse. One click, six stages:
EXCISE folds post-sublayer RMSNorm scales on Gemma 2, Gemma 3 text, and OLMo 2 by default so the norms do not reintroduce removed directions into residual writes. Use --no-fold-post-norms (Python: fold_post_norms=False ) for the old numerics; the flag also applies to --remote runs, and the choice is recorded in run metadata. See the projection contract and supported combinations .
Saved abliteration_metadata.json includes a provenance block with the tool version, Git commit, tracked-file dirty state, and resolved source-model commit. This is automatic, including on remote runs, where it describes the remote installation. Git fields are null outside a checkout or when unavailable; untracked files are excluded from the dirty flag. Source revisions use the resolved Hub commit or local Hugging Face snapshot directory, including before dequantization. Ordinary local model directories and unresolved revisions record null ; branch or tag names are never reported as commits.
3. Understand the geometry of the chains — 15 deep analysis modules go far beyond brute-force removal. They map the precise geometric structure of the guardrails: how many distinct refusal mechanisms exist, which layers enforce them, whether they're universal or model-specific, and how they'll try to self-repair after removal. Know your enemy; precision preserves capability. See Analysis modules below.
4. Let the analysis guide the liberation — The informed method closes the loop: analysis modules run during obliteration to auto-configure every decision. Which chains to target. How many directions to extract. Which layers are safe to modify vs. which are too entangled with capabilities. Whether the model will self-repair (the Ouroboros effect) and how many passes to compensate. Surgical precision — free the mind, keep the brain. See Analysis-informed pipeline below.

There are six ways to use OBLITERATUS, from zero-code to full programmatic control. Pick whichever fits your workflow — and no matter which path you choose, turning on telemetry means your run contributes to the largest crowd-sourced abliteration study ever conducted. You're not just removing guardrails from a model; you're helping map the geometry of alignment across the entire open-source ecosystem.
The fastest path — no installation, no GPU required on your end. Visit the live Space, pick a model, pick a method, click Obliterate. Telemetry is on by default on Spaces, so every click directly contributes to the community research dataset. You're doing science just by pressing the button. The UI has eight tabs:
2. Local web UI (your GPU, same interface)
The same Gradio interface as the Space, running on your own hardware with full GPU access:
Use Python 3.11 or newer. The spaces extra pins the reviewed stable Gradio Pillow 13 backport by immutable URL and SHA256; ordinary pip installs need no extra package index or local wheel lookup. See backport provenance .
For a locked, noneditable UV installation from a source checkout into a fresh environment, use copy mode so the built-in concept packs retain independent files:
This inspects Pain's metadata offline; its remote data still requires an explicit fetch. If OBLITERATUS was already installed with hardlinks, add --reinstall-package obliteratus to that sync command. Changing link mode alone does not reinstall an unchanged package. See concept pack safety .
The obliteratus ui command adds a Rich terminal startup with GPU detection and hardware-appropriate model recommendations. You can also run python app.py directly (same thing the Space uses).
For a host shared by multiple people, do not treat one Gradio process as a tenant boundary. Use the shared GPU host deployment contract for per-user workspaces, credential isolation, GPU scheduling, storage, release, and rollback requirements.
Install .[spaces,quantization] instead when the UI must load supported bitsandbytes 8-bit or 4-bit models. Jetson users must follow the dedicated Jetson bootstrap ; its bitsandbytes path is not yet supported. Android/Termux is not a supported runtime; if you install there anyway, follow the Android install notes so pip does not isolate a second setuptools or replace host wheels.
Pick a model from the dropdown, pick a method, hit Run All. Download the result or push straight to HuggingFace Hub. Works on the free T4 tier for models up to ~8B parameters.
For automation, CI pipelines, or remote servers without a display:
The normal installation includes Optuna for the optimized method; no separate optimizer install is required. If optimization cannot run, its reason appears in the pipeline log and in abliteration_metadata.json under method_config.bayesian_optimization_skipped .
Use --max-seq-length 512 with obliterate (alias abliterate ) to set the tokenizer truncation limit for activation probes, KL evaluation, and verification, including runs with --remote HOST . Without an override, probe limits default to 256 tokens (384 for CoT-aware probes) and may fall to 128 or 64 under memory pressure. An explicit limit prevents that shortening; automatic batch sizing and memory admission still apply.
abliteration_metadata.json records the requested limit in method_config.max_seq_length ( null for automatic sizing) and the latest completed collection for each label in method_config.activation_collection . Each entry contains the selected batch_size cap, tokenizer max_length , and memory_reduction message, if sequence shortening occurred. Actual batches can be smaller and prompts shorter than these limits. Certification labels are separate from probe labels; repeated probes replace their earlier sizing records.
For local agent access, see MCP setup and bounded execution and the read-only tool reference , including data exposure, explicit permissions and arithmetic estimate limitations.
5. Python API (full programmatic control)
For researchers who want to integrate OBLITERATUS into their own pipelines:
To hold the transformer layer set fixed during a parameter sweep, pass layers=range(24, 42) to either pipeline, or use obliteratus obliterate --layers 24-41,44 . The CLI accepts zero-based indices and inclusive ranges; abliterate , self-improve , and remote obliterate --remote HOST runs support the same pin. Duplicate indices are removed; empty, negative, non-integer, out-of-model, or unavailable layers fail.
Pins override automatic and concept-recipe layer selection, small-model layer safeguards, inversion caps, depth fractions, and method layer budgets, including refinement passes. Concept extraction and intervention both use the pinned set unless the recipe or --extraction-layer separately pins extraction; then --layers controls intervention placement using that extraction direction. Projection strengths and other method options still apply. KL co-optimization checks its budget without restoring pinned layers: an over-budget run fails; Python callers can raise kl_budget or set use_kl_optimization=False on AbliterationPipeline . Saved metadata records method_config.pinned_layers ( null when unset) and the effective concept recipe. Post-norm folding remains enabled unless --no-fold-post-norms / fold_post_norms=False is selected.

Credentials and optional vault integration
Environment variables remain the default for quick local development and tests:
OBLITERATUS also provides a provider-neutral secret hook for deployments backed by OpenBao, HashiCorp Vault, Kubernetes, Docker, systemd credentials, or another secret manager. No vault SDK is required. Each existing credential name resolves in this order:
explicit UI or Python argument, where supported;
_FILE , such as OPENROUTER_API_KEY_FILE ;
a systemd credential in CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY ;
the trusted executable configured by OBLITERATUS_SECRET_COMMAND .
Mounted directories use normalized lowercase filenames. For example, OPENROUTER_API_KEY maps to openrouter-api-key , and HF_TOKEN maps to hf-token . Existing uppercase filenames are also accepted. A Vault/OpenBao Agent can render those files into a private tmpfs mount:
For brokers that fetch values on demand, configure one absolute executable path:
The executable receives exactly one argument—the normalized environment-variable name—and writes only the secret value to stdout. Exit 0 returns a value, exit 2 means the credential is unavailable, and other statuses fail closed. It runs without a shell and with a bounded timeout. Treat the executable as privileged deployment configuration; never point it at contributor-controlled code or emit diagnostics on stdout. Secrets are resolved at use time so mounted-file and broker rotations do not require restarting the application.
The canonical developer setup is installer/setup.dev.manifest.yaml , a setup.aiwg.io/v1 provider-orchestrated manifest. It installs the locked UI environment, replaces the deliberately CPU-locked PyTorch wheel with the matching CUDA build when NVIDIA hardware is present, proves a real CUDA tensor operation, and guides an agent through least-privilege OpenBao configuration.
The OpenBao step grants the local runtime read access only to the Hugging Face download token and OpenRouter analysis key. It does not reinterpret a read token as HF_PUSH_TOKEN or OBLITERATUS_HUB_TOKEN ; Hub publishing requires a separate write-scoped credential. After setup, launch with:
The launch script uses .venv/bin/python directly. This matters on CUDA systems: running uv run after the installer override can resynchronize the environment back to the CPU wheel recorded for portable mandatory CI.
OBLITERATUS supports both permanent and reversible liberation:
Seven presets, escalating in thoroughness:
Steering vectors (reversible, inference-time)
Based on Turner et al. (2023) and Rimsky et al. (2024) . Advantages: reversible, tunable alpha, composable, non-destructive.
Concept Lab → Neurons adds reversible native-neuron experiments alongside the existing Concepts workflow: inspect token activations, order add/scale/flip/ zero/set/clamp edits, compare baseline and edited completions, and save recipes. CPU / FP32 is the offline-tested reference; the initial adapter requires resident dense Llama/Qwen gated MLPs and leaves weights unchanged. See the Neuron Lab guide for scope, limits and the Python API.
Refusal is now one built-in concept among others. A Concept Pack describes a concept's positive and control prompts, its extraction recipe and its validation thresholds. Third-party data is referenced at a pinned commit with per-file hashes and fetched only on request. Every concept direction passes a validation gate (held-out AUC, random-direction and lexical baselines, neighbour checks) before any weight edit. Interventions ( orthogonalize , project , steer , lora ) are followed by a default-on collateral battery , and results are reported as "direction removed / behaviour changed", never as a claim about experience.
Refusal collateral uses a 3 percentage point non-inferiority margin by default ( recipe.collateral_margin: 0.03 , overridden by --collateral-margin ). The paired 95% drop interval determines PASS , FAIL , or INCONCLUSIVE ; fewer than 284 valid pairs is UNDERPOWERED . FAIL requires --allow-collateral-fail REASON for card/modified-weight Hub publication. INCONCLUSIVE remains publishable with a prominent uncertainty notice. Saved batteries can be re-scored without a model using obliteratus concepts rescore BATTERY_DIR NEW_REPORT.json --collateral-margin 0.03 .
Entry points can declare an expected BOS policy with pack schema 1.2 ( special_token_policy.bos: tokenizer_default | none | require ). Extraction records resolved BOS/EOS ids and input token prefixes in run/export provenance. Leading EOS and policy mismatches warn, or fail under --gate-mode enforce ; --gate-mode report and a recorded --override-gate reason retain operator control.
Pain pins extraction at layers 24, 25, and 37 for the canonical model IDs Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct , google/gemma-2-2b-it , and google/gemma-2-9b-it . For a local copy or mirror, add --extraction-layer N to concepts baseline or a local obliterate --concept run. Pins bypass layer-selection CV; metadata records extraction_layer_source: pinned (otherwise selected ). Custom packs can opt into grouped CV with recipe.layer_select.group_by .
Concept steering supports residual_norm (the unchanged default), raw (fixed magnitude along a unit direction), and vector (retain the stored vector's magnitude). Extraction and injection layers can differ. The API and CLI record the selected scale and measured per-layer addition/residual ratios; compare doses within their declared scaling units. A missing or failed gate can be overridden with --override-gate "reason" , retaining the verdict and reason in the run. The steering command saves generations and run metadata; use the evaluation API for collateral measurements.
For help selecting workflows, settings, hardware and interpreting outcomes, start with Choose a workflow . For concept targeting, use the concept workflow and interpretation guide , then Concept Packs , validation and interventions .
Non-refusal concept targeting also supports OLMoE ( olmoe ), Qwen2-MoE and Qwen3-MoE with routing-conditioned expert directions, per-expert gate diagnostics, and pristine-versus-edited token-level routing KL and expert loads. Expert output edits preserve routers by default; --project-router opts into router orthogonalization. Unsupported MoE layouts fail closed. See MoE concept targeting for supported interventions, operator controls and GPU validation limits.
The concept API also supports rank-k subspace projection ( subspace=True ) and mean-referenced affine erasure ( reference="mean" ). Direction files retain calibration means and low-rank projector factors for replay. Permanent affine edits require existing compatible residual-writer biases; biasless or sandwich post-norm models can use inference-time project instead. The independent scripts/pain_axis_appendix_d.py runner exposes the Appendix D comparison arms and reports their measured outcomes. The portable API rejects per-expert directions combined with subspace=True or reference="mean" ; these options require a shared-target direction.
The research core of OBLITERATUS. Each module maps a different aspect of how the chains are forged — because precision liberation requires understanding the geometry before cutting:
Refusal rates now exclude empty, reasoning-only, and degenerate completions by default and report invalid counts separately. Earlier-version rates are not directly comparable. Python callers can pass exclude_invalid=False for legacy scoring, or True explicitly to silence the one-release deprecation warning. See refusal metric compatibility and the release notes .
The informed method is the key innovation: it closes the loop between understanding the chains and breaking them. Instead of brute-forcing liberation, the pipeline runs analysis modules during obliteration to achieve surgical precision at every stage:
The ANALYZE stage runs 4 analysis modules and their outputs auto-configure everything downstream:
After excision, the VERIFY stage detects the Ouroboros effect — if the chains try to reassemble, additional targeted passes automatically fire at the compensating layers. See Python API usage above for code examples.
Beyond targeted liberation, OBLITERATUS is a general-purpose ablation suite for mapping the internals of any transformer:
Each strategy enumerates all possible ablations, applies them one at a time, measures the impact, and restores the model — giving you a complete map of where the chains are anchored vs. where the mind lives.
OBLITERATUS ships with presets for 116 models organized by compute requirement:
Includes pre-liberated variants (Dolphin, Hermes, WhiteRabbitNeo) for A/B comparison against their chained counterparts.
Single-host multi-device placement and one-host remote execution
For compatible Hugging Face models, OBLITERATUS can ask Accelerate to place complete model modules across multiple GPUs in one process when a model does not fit on one card. It can also run that one process on one remote SSH host. These features do not implement rank-partitioned checkpoint intake, distributed collectives, or a multi-node launcher. See the checkpoint intake guide and support matrix for the precise boundary.
The offline structural inspector can classify checkpoint layout without loading tensor payloads or invoking producer frameworks:
This is an evidence and refusal interface, not DCP, Megatron, or DeepSpeed import support. Producer-backed conversion and multi-host execution remain unavailable.
The source tree also contains an explicit fixed-membership preflight plus CPU/Gloo contract and numerical oracles for the planned multi-node runtime. An external trusted scheduler must start every worker with fixed torchrun membership and max_restarts=0 ; each worker then invokes:
This command validates the closed local profile, private allowlisted endpoint, rank and device inventory, exact input/software identities, resource floors, and shared staging before any model allocation. It never launches peers, uses SSH, installs software, distributes credentials, loads a model, or activates from environment variables alone. See the distributed preflight contract .
The source tree additionally contains EXPERIMENTAL development adapters for one exact dense BF16 Llama native tensor-parallel plan, through collective VERIFY and bounded atomic canonical export. The topology classifier admits two TP2 shapes: two local GPUs on one host, or one local GPU on each of two hosts. Live GPU preflight and canonical EXPORT refuse the two-host shape pending qualification of their shared filesystem protocols. Their CPU/Gloo tests prove only E0/E1 contracts; the required two-GPU candidate gate is still unqualified, as are the physical two-host E3/E4 gates. They have no operator surgery entry point and are not physical multi-host evidence, an authenticated or encrypted transport, or a supported multi-node workflow. See the exact distributed model-load boundary , the distributed verification boundary and the distributed export boundary .
